title: OpenTelemetry demo checkout
scope: The checkout journey from the storefront: the checkout form submit, the Next.js POST /api/checkout route, and the Go CheckoutService.PlaceOrder orchestration including cart, product catalog, currency, payment, shipping, email and the orders Kafka event. Downstream services are contracts at the boundary; do not map their internal implementations.
hints: CheckoutForm.tsx submits the form; pages/cart/index.tsx wires it to the API route.
src/frontend/pages/api/checkout.ts is the HTTP entrypoint; it calls Checkout.gateway.placeOrder and hydrates the response with ProductCatalogService.
src/checkout/main.go implements CheckoutService.PlaceOrder and orchestrates cart, product catalog, currency, payment, shipping and email over gRPC.
Cart data is stored in Valkey by src/cart; the checkout service reads and empties it through CartService.
src/checkout/kafka/producer.go publishes the OrderResult to the orders topic when a broker is configured.
pb/demo.proto defines the request, cart, money, order and response shapes used across the flow.
rubric: This is a two-boundary flow: the storefront submits the form, POST /api/checkout forwards the PlaceOrderRequest to the checkout gRPC service, and CheckoutService.PlaceOrder orchestrates the order. Model the UI form, the HTTP route and the gRPC method as separate EntryPoints; the form reaches the route through a directional RELATED edge, and the route relates to the gRPC method. Put each flow in the cluster of the code that owns it (frontend and checkout-service) and use the downstream services only as boundary contracts: cart-service, product-catalog, currency-service, payment-service, shipping-service, email-service and kafka. The cart storage is Valkey; the orders topic is a queue, not an external service. Outbound gRPC clients inside checkout are participants, not EntryPoints. Penalize one cluster per node, invented services or queues, and splitting cache/conditional branches into extra flows.
